judgment.rationale: A normal namespace-folder open should not be attributed to a shortcut collision solely because Palette appears. Compare ordinary folder opening and direct namespace activation with Palette enabled/disabled to determine whether the shell association/namespace route or Palette activation is involved. No root cause or registry repair is established; unsafe association resets are not justified.

comment.body: Thanks for the supplied archive and screenshots; they already show the GodMode namespace suffix, the Palette window and Windows26H2 build26300.9711. To isolate the launch path, please compare opening an ordinary folder and the GodMode namespace directly from the Explorer address bar using `shell:::{ED7BA470-8E54-465E-825C-99712043E01C}`. Then disable only Command Palette and repeat those two opens plus the original GodMode-folder double-click. Please report which opens change behavior; this is a behavior comparison only, not a request for additional diagnostics or registry changes.

Repeat on the supplied Windows build and a supported comparison build if the behavior is build-specific.

plan: Compare ordinary folders, the existing GodMode folder and direct Explorer namespace navigation with Palette enabled and disabled.

Correct only the demonstrated registration/activation conflict and regression-test standard folder/namespace behavior; do not reset user shell associations speculatively.
